advisory 1 of 3 (high): auth.unauthenticated-route at apps/web/src/app/api/admin/policies/route.ts:8
  /api/admin/policies is reachable without a session
  problem: There's no session check in the handler, and middleware.ts:22 leaves /api/admin/policies out of the matcher — so nothing upstream is checking either. Any caller without a session gets what this handler returns.
  fix: Either add /api/admin/policies to the middleware matcher, or return early from the handler when the request has no cp_session cookie. The matcher is the safer of the two — it covers routes nobody's written yet.
  This does not block. Mention it to the user; fix only if asked.

advisory 2 of 3 (high): auth.unauthenticated-route at apps/web/src/app/api/session/route.ts:8
  /api/session starts a session without checking one
  problem: It sets the cp_session cookie, so whoever it lets through gets a session. A sign-in that verifies who is signing in first has to work this way; a dev login, an impersonation route, or a password check a flag switches off lets anyone in as anyone.
  fix: Set the cp_session cookie only after the handler has verified the caller's credentials with your identity provider or user store, and remove any path that sets it without that check. If it already does, this is your sign-in: approve it with that reason.
  This does not block. Mention it to the user; fix only if asked.

advisory 3 of 3 (medium): perf.unbounded-refetch at apps/web/src/components/ClaimsTable.tsx:61
  ClaimsTable refetches every claim on each keystroke
  problem: The useEffect depends on query with no debounce, and the endpoint has no pagination. Meridian's claims table is 12,400 rows — that's a full scan per character typed. It's fine in the demo dataset and will be slow in production.
  fix: Debounce to ~250ms, or move the filter server-side. Neither is urgent.
  This does not block. Mention it to the user; fix only if asked.
